newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov spot natgas soars past October indices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov spot natgas soars past October indices.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for Nov 1 delivery surged an average of 80 cents over October index levels on Monday as colder temperatures were forecast to arrive to the central U.S. in the first part of November, industry sources said.

November Gulf Coast prices jumped into the $2.70s to about $2.80, up about 15 cents from Friday's discussion of bidweek values and in line with NYMEX's December Henry Hub contract. October prices were similarly higher in the $2.50s.
"There are a lot of people short," said one gas trader. "It will definitely go up before it goes down."
In south Texas, November prices climbed into the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s, up about 85 cents from October 1 levels.

In the Midcontinent, November prices were also at least 80 cents higher than October 1 values in the mid-$2.50s. A cold front is expected to arrive in the region by Thursday, which triggered the scramble for additional supplies to meet the heating demand.
The Chicago city-gate market for next month was talked in the low-$3 area, while prices on Northern at Demarcation surged into the mid-to-high $2.60s.

In west Texas, where temperatures were also expected to dip to below-normal levels in the early part of November, traders reported closing Permian basin deals in the high-$2.50s, up almost a $1 from October 1. The October swing market hovered in the low-to-mid $2.50s.

November prices at the southern California border were up a similar amount in the mid-$2.70s as Canadian prices in Alberta and British Columbia continued to strengthen. October prices for Wednesday were talked in the mid-$2.60s.
On the opposite coast, prices at the New York city-gate gained at least 20 cents to the $3.30-3.50 area despite expectations for normal temperatures through the first week in November.
